prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the 3D geometry of the corner kitchen, separating the near foreground—the person in the maroon hoodie (bright white/light grey at roughly 0.4 to 1.0 m, within the camera wearer's arm's reach from frame 2 onward) and the vertical partition wall entering on the left in frames 3 to 5 (0.4 to 0.7 m away, also within arm's reach)—from the mid-ground upper cabinets, range hood, and countertop microwave (medium grey at roughly 1.2 to 2.0 m, within the other person's arm's reach) and the dark background ceiling and adjacent room beyond the partition (over 2.5 m away). Across the five frames, the increasing brightness and scale of the person and the left wall edge show the camera wearer panning left and approaching from about 1.0 m to 0.5 m while the person shifts from the lower-left edge toward the center-right and turns their head from facing away (frames 1–3) to profile (frame 4) to facing the camera wearer (frame 5). The depth map clearly reveals the continuous planar recession of the intersecting cabinet walls, the protruding box volume of the corner microwave, and the sharp depth discontinuity between the foreground partition wall and the deeper room to its left, which are harder to judge quantitatively from RGB alone. However, the map is unreliable in assigning noticeably darker (farther) values to the person's head than to their hoodie shoulders, bleeding depth halos around the motion-blurred head in frame 3, and flattening small countertop objects like the dish rack and bottles into the background.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and countertop objects against an unlabelled black background, detecting the person in the lower foreground (roughly 0.4 to 1.0 m from the camera wearer, cropped at the chest/shoulders by the bottom frame border) alongside kitchen items situated about 0.5 to 1.0 m behind the person. In frame 1, the person at the bottom-left partially occludes a purple mask over the white range hood above them (~1.2 m away); in frame 2, as the person shifts right into full view (~0.7 m away, facing away from the camera wearer), the map delineates a cyan bottle (~1.2 m away, just to the right of the person's shoulder and within their arm's reach), a purple microwave (~1.5 m away in the corner), and a bowl on top of the microwave; in frame 4, it detects a green 'sink' mask at the bottom-right (~1.2 m away) as the person turns their head right; and in frame 5, only the close-up person (~0.5 m away, looking back at the camera wearer) is segmented. These pixel-level masks make it easy to separate overlapping silhouettes—such as the narrow bottle between the person's right shoulder and the microwave in frame 2—that blend into the cluttered countertop in RGB. However, the map is unreliable across frames: it completely misses all objects during the motion blur of frame 3, misclassifies the overhead range hood as a 'microwave' in frame 1 and a 'tv' in frame 2, mislabels the corner microwave area as a 'sink' in frame 4, and omits the cabinets, partition wall, and countertop clutter.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is almost entirely blank across the five frames, rendering only sparse, fragmented yellow body keypoints in frames 2 and 4 and no magenta hand skeletons in any frame. Because the person stands very close to the camera wearer (roughly 0.4 to 1.0 m away) and is occluded below the upper chest by the bottom border of the egocentric view, their arms and hands remain completely out of view below the frame even though the kitchen counter and bottle (~0.4 to 0.6 m in front of them) are within their arm's reach. In frame 2, a partial yellow shoulder-and-neck structure appears near the bottom-left where the person faces away toward the range hood, and in frame 4, a small cluster of tangled yellow torso/head segments appears near the bottom-center as the person turns their head to the right, while frames 1, 3, and 5 contain zero detections despite the person looking directly at the camera wearer from ~0.5 m away in frame 5. While the sparse detections in frames 2 and 4 roughly confirm the person's horizontal shift from left to center-right in the lower foreground, the pose map adds no spatial detail beyond the RGB image and is highly unreliable under severe lower-body truncation, back-facing orientations, and motion blur.
